attempts.label: DANDI:001526
attempts.paper_title: Sub-microsecond optical measurements of cell membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields
attempts.entry_title: Membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields in CHO cells (Semenov et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Few of the paper's findings could be tested, and none held up cleanly. The dandiset holds only the Di-8-ANEPPS alternating-field and short-pulse experiments, so the FluoVolt, Gd3+, calcium and two-pulse recovery findings could not be tested. Stable responses before electroporation did not reproduce, and the lasting drop afterwards was larger than reported, both depending on an undescribed background subtraction and on which cells the paper used. The fall in polarization within a set at the electroporating field held only under one background choice made after seeing results. The maximum polarization with short pulses reached 34.9% against the reported 53%.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Silkuniene, Silkunas, Pakhomova, Bixler, Ibey, Kochunov and Pakhomov (2026) on dandiset 001526, which holds Di-8-ANEPPS strobe images of 19 CHO cells, the alternating 150 and 230 V/cm protocol around a 1000 V/cm exposure (Fig. 2C and D) and the 0.3 us escalation (Fig. 4D). It traces each cell's membrane, measures pole dF per image and per set, and evaluates Eq. (2). The FluoVolt, 1 us escalation, Gd3+, Ca2+ and two-pulse experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Semenov et al. (2026) from dandiset 001526

outcomes.statement: Repeated alternating sets of 150 and 230 V/cm PEFs produced dF responses that stayed constant within each set and between sets, so that 800 flashes and 480 pulses had no obvious impact before the 1000 V/cm exposure.
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 4; Figure 2C and D
outcomes.quote: Repeated sets of PEFs at 150 and 230 V/cm, delivered in alternation, produced ΔF responses that stayed constant both within each set and between the sets (Fig. 2C and D).
outcomes.notes: Paired t-tests of each pre-exposure 150 or 230 V/cm set against the first set of its field, per pole, n = 11 cells (10 for the fourth 230 V/cm set). With each cell's background recording subtracted (adopted), 1 of 12 comparisons has p < 0.05, the third 150 V/cm set at the cathodic pole, 10.8% against 17.6% (p = 0.031). The annulus and darkest-pixel readings also give 1 of 12 (p = 0.045 and 0.038); without subtraction none (smallest p 0.055), which would reproduce the claim. F0 from images 2 to 40 gives 3 of 12 with the background recording. At the cathodic pole every later pre-exposure 150 V/cm set is 27 to 39% below the first, the 230 V/cm sets -11.9 to 4.7%. Within sets, the first and last 10 PEF images differ by at most 1.15% (p 0.39 or more). The outcome rests on the cells: without c3 and c4, the two whose pre-exposure sets depart from the described order, no comparison differs under any reading (smallest p 0.067, background recording), and among the 165 choices of 8 of the 11 cells none differs in 76 (background recording), 80 (annulus), 83 (floor) and 100 (none). With per-cell pole angles 2 of 12 differ. Whether the right cells were picked is open: c4, c8 and c10 have first 150 V/cm cathodic sets of 3.4 to 3.8%, against 5.0 to 15.3% for their later pre-exposure 150 V/cm sets, and c4 has the weakest cosine amplitude of the session (4.28). The result is weak, one uncorrected test of 12. The criterion is binary (not reproduced when any set differs); the background reading and the choice of cells are put to the paper's authors (findings).
deviations: Background subtraction is an assumption. Section 2.3 describes dF = 100 (F - F0)/F0 with no background step, section 2.4 subtracts the background fluorescence of a cell-free region for Fluo-4, and the claims file names both readings. The adopted reading subtracts, for 2025-05-01, the mean of the cell-free background recording made with each cell (the files call it a recording in the background region without cells, so the experimenters recorded it with every cell of that session), point by point along the trace; for 2025-05-06, which has no background recordings, the per-image median of a cell-free annulus 2 to 3 radii from the cell, whose level the background recordings of the first session match within 0.97 to 1.08 times. Cell-free background is 52 to 54% of the trace intensity, and 65 to 66 counts above the darkest pixels (no dark frame or camera offset is given), and the paper's own values at 1000 V/cm (40 and 26.6%) are on the scale of the subtracted readings and about 3 times the unsubtracted ones (40/13.3 = 3.0 and 26.6/8.5 = 3.1 under window (b)). The notebook shows every reading (background recording, annulus, darkest-pixel floor, none). Round 1 adopted the annulus for both sessions; the background recording was adopted in the revision after round 1, after the results under both readings had been seen, and in that revision the annulus reading stopped meeting fig2c-1000-within-set while the background recording met it. The choice is to be read as made after the results.

The analysed cell is the one nearest the image centre of the cell's sham recording (an assumption; the files do not say which of the one to eight cells found in each field was analysed, and section 2.2 centres the field of view between the electrodes). The notebook draws every traced membrane on its baseline image.

The 6-pixel-wide perimeter trace is found automatically as the outer ridge of the membrane staining in the sham recording's baseline image and moved by the measured drift (at most 2 pixels), where the paper draws it by hand in MetaMorph (section 2.3); the 360 points are spaced by 1 degree of angle, not by equal arc length. For 2025-05-01 c4 the default rule (steepest outward fall) put the trace on internal staining (median radius 21.2 px), so that cell is traced with the outermost strong fall (34.1 px); the other cells keep the default rule, which the overlays show on the membrane (c3's trace cuts inside the cell on one side, away from the poles).

The cathodic pole angle is the median over the session's cells of the phase of a cosine fitted to the polarization profile at non-electroporating fields (83.0 degrees for 1 us, 82.1 degrees for 0.3 us, close to straight up, as in Fig. 1); the paper places the poles by the field direction. Per-cell phases (73.1 to 93.6 degrees) are shown as a variant.

Field strengths are the paper's labels (Fig. 2C; the Fig. 4D axis labels 357, 760, 1000, 1200, 1420, 1630, 2050, 2473 and 3320 V/cm, read from the figure on page 6 of the PDF) matched by order to the pulse amplitudes in volts that the files give; the labels are not proportional to the volts.

11 cells are used where the paper reports n = 8; the dataset does not say which 8. Four cells depart from the described order of sets (c3 and c4 before the 1000 V/cm exposure, c1 and c11 after); sets are matched by their rank at each field. The notebook applies the criteria without c4, without c3 and c4, without all four, and to every choice of 8 of the 11 cells.
The fifth pre-exposure 150 V/cm set exists in one cell only and is not tested.

outcomes.statement: At 1000 V/cm, cathodic pole dF fell from 40 +- 10% at the start of the set to 26.6 +- 8% at its end, a trend that was not statistically significant.
outcomes.quote: In contrast, at an electroporating field strength of 1000 V/cm, ΔF at the cathodic pole decreased from 40 ± 10% at the beginning of the set to 26.6 ± 8% at the end of it. Although not statistically significant (p > 0.05)

outcomes.statement: Set-averaged dF stayed nearly constant before electroporation but dropped by about 20% (a small but persistent reduction of at most 20%) in the 150 and 230 V/cm sets acquired after the 1000 V/cm exposure.
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 4; Figure 2D and legend
outcomes.quote: ΔF values averaged across each set of 60 PEFs stayed nearly constant before the electroporation, but dropped by about 20% in the sets acquired after it (Fig. 2D, p < 0.05).
outcomes.notes: Measured is the mean reduction over the four post-exposure sets of both poles' |dF| averaged (readings b and i), background recording subtracted. Per set 30.3, 28.8, 26.1 and 23.8% (p = 0.017, 0.018, 0.019, 0.094). Under every background and F0 reading the both-pole mean is 26.9 to 28.1% and no set with p < 0.05 has a reduction within 18 to 22%. At single poles the drop is at the cathodic pole for 150 V/cm (49.5 and 43.1%, p = 0.017 and 0.026) and at the anodic pole for 230 V/cm (32.4 and 33.3%, p = 0.051 and 0.109). The only per-pole mean within 18 to 22% is the anodic pole with F0 from images 2 to 40 and the annulus (18.7%), an average of set reductions of 2.3 to 30.4% that comes with a pre-exposure set at p = 0.029, so it does not meet the reproduced clause, and the partial clause (size outside the tolerance under every reading) is not literally met there either; partial is the closer description, as every both-pole set size is outside the tolerance with the session pole angle; the round-1 pass of this kind (annulus, anodic, 18.0%) is gone with c4 re-traced (17.4%). The criterion's condition that no pre-exposure set differs fails under the adopted reading (p = 0.031) and holds without subtraction. The reduction is significant under every reading and larger than about 20%, the partial case the criterion names. Without c3 and c4 the criterion is met under the background recording, annulus and no-subtraction readings; among the 165 choices of 8 cells it is met in 2 (background recording), and in 16 more the size is met with a pre-exposure set that differs, which meets neither clause; without all four protocol-breaking cells (n = 7) no post-exposure set reaches p < 0.05.

outcomes.statement: With 0.3 us PEFs at 357 to 3320 V/cm (imaged at 275 ns), the maximum dF was 53 +- 4% (about 600 mV) at both poles, similar to 1 us pulses, and its pattern with increasing field strength did not differ from that with 1 us pulses.
outcomes.quote: Contrary to the expectations, the results were similar to those with 1-μs pulses ... the maximum ΔF reached was 53 ± 4% (~600 mV) at both cell poles. The pattern of how the response changed with increasing PEF strength was not different from that with 1-μs PEFs either.
outcomes.notes: Measured is the larger of the two pole maxima. Annulus background (the session has no background recordings), maximum mean |dF| 34.9% at the cathodic pole (1200 V/cm) and 34.0% at the anodic pole (1630 V/cm); darkest-pixel floor 26.6 and 26.5%; without subtraction 15.0% and 16.7%; all outside 49 to 57%. Per cell, the maxima span 18.8 to 52.4% (cathodic) and 24.1 to 49.9% (anodic); three of 8 cells reach 49.6 to 52.4% at the cathodic pole. The pattern part holds under every reading; |dF| falls at every step beyond the maximum, by 82% (cathodic) and 49% (anodic) of the maximum at 3320 V/cm. Both poles' maxima are out of tolerance, so the outcome is not the partial case. The dataset holds 8 of the paper's 10 cells, so no choice of cells can be tested; the two missing cells would each need |dF| above 100% to bring the mean into range, so the outcome does not rest on the background reading or the choice of cells.

outcomes.statement: By Eq. (2), effective membrane conductivity has little effect on charging while it stays much smaller than the cytosol and medium conductivities; a 10-fold increase gives about a 2% IMP reduction and a 100-fold increase about 12%.
outcomes.quote: As expected, effective conductivity had little impact on charging for as long as it remained much smaller than the cytosol and media conductivities ... its 10-fold increase would go unnoticed, yielding just a ~2% IMP reduction, and a 100-fold increase would reduce IMP by just 12%.
outcomes.notes: Eq. (2) as printed in the PDF gives f = 1.498 at the intact conductivity. 100-fold increase 11.87% reduction (11.75% against f at the intact value), within 10.8 to 13.2%. 10-fold increase 1.33% (1.20%), outside 1.8 to 2.2%; a 2% reduction needs about a 15-fold increase. The criterion gives no partial case; one of two values matching is recorded as partial.
deviations: Eq. (2) is read from the PDF, as the extracted text garbles it.

outcomes.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS and 1 us PEFs, polarization depolarizes the cathode-facing pole and hyperpolarizes the anode-facing pole, falls off towards the equator and scales with field strength up to 570 V/cm; at 780 V/cm the cathodic pole stops increasing and dims; at 1000 to 1400 V/cm the poles show reduced or absent polarization while regions nearer the equator remain polarized and may exceed the poles.
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.1, paragraph 1; Figure 1 and legend
outcomes.quote: At a higher electric field strength of 780 V/cm, polarization at the cathodic pole does not further increase but dims out, indicating a less efficient charging of the partially permeabilized membrane. Still stronger electric fields produce a distinct pattern of reduced or absent polarization at the poles
outcomes.notes: Needs the Di-8-ANEPPS 1 us escalation from 43 to 1400 V/cm (the Fig. 4B group, n = 5); the dandiset holds 1 us recordings only at 150, 230 and 1000 V/cm, in the alternating protocol of Fig. 2C, and the paper's data availability statement says data are available on request.

outcomes.statement: In FluoVolt-loaded cells, pole dF rose with field strength until apparent saturation at 66% (255 mV) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole and -83% (-320 mV) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole; stronger fields did not increase the anodic response and decreased the cathodic one.
outcomes.quote: ΔF increased proportionally to the electric field strength until reaching apparent saturation at 66% ΔF (255 mV IMP) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole, and −83% ΔF (−320 mV IMP) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole. Further escalation of the electric field strength did not increase the dye response at the anodic pole and even decreased it at the cathodic pole.
outcomes.notes: Needs FluoVolt recordings; every file in the dandiset is Di-8-ANEPPS (its description says so).

outcomes.statement: Without PEF (the first 40 images of each set) FluoVolt measurements were stable, showing no significant photosensitization or dye bleaching.
outcomes.quote: Without PEF (first 40 datapoints, or ~ 7 s in each set), measurements were stable, indicating no significant photosensitization or dye bleaching.
outcomes.notes: Needs FluoVolt recordings; every file in the dandiset is Di-8-ANEPPS (its description says so).

outcomes.statement: At 1000 V/cm and above, which strongly electroporated the cells, the FluoVolt response stayed stable through the 60 pulses of each set.
outcomes.quote: Field strengths of 1000 V/cm and higher caused strong electroporation (see Section 3.5), but the dye response in each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses applied
outcomes.notes: Needs FluoVolt recordings; every file in the dandiset is Di-8-ANEPPS (its description says so).

outcomes.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS has a lower sensitivity than FluoVolt, but its dF kept rising with field strength up to 570 V/cm at both poles.
outcomes.quote: This dye has a lower sensitivity to membrane polarization (note the vertical scale different from Fig. 2A), but ΔF kept climbing up to the electric field strength of 570 V/cm at both cell poles.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Fig. 2B Di-8-ANEPPS escalation from 43 to 1400 V/cm, not in the dandiset. The FluoVolt comparison is missing as well.

outcomes.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS responses were somewhat affected by bleaching, most noticeably at 43 V/cm, where bleaching added about 5% to dF at the anodic pole and reduced it by about 5% at the cathodic pole.
outcomes.quote: The responses were somewhat affected by dye bleaching (particularly noticeable at 43 V/cm, where bleaching added ~5% to ΔF at the anodic pole and reduced it by the same ~5% at the cathodic pole.
outcomes.notes: Needs the 43 V/cm set of the Fig. 2B escalation, not in the dandiset (no 43 V/cm recordings at all).

outcomes.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS responses to PEFs at and above 780 V/cm decreased gradually within each set of 60 images.
outcomes.quote: In addition, responses to PEFs at and above 780 V/cm decreased gradually in each set of 60 images, consistent with expectations of adding membrane damage by additional electroporation pulses in each set
outcomes.notes: Needs the 780 to 1400 V/cm sets of the Fig. 2B escalation, not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Fitting dF against IMPC from -150 to +150 mV with a line through the origin gave slopes of 26% (FluoVolt) and 9.1% (Di-8-ANEPPS) dF per 100 mV, with correlation coefficients of 0.96 and 0.78.
outcomes.quote: The correlation coefficients of the fits equaled 0.96 for FluoVolt and 0.78 for Di-8 ANEPPS (due to a lower signal-to-noise ratio), with respective slope coefficients of 26% and 9.1% ΔF per 100 mV of IMP.
outcomes.notes: Needs the FluoVolt calibration cells, not in the dandiset, so the criterion (both slopes) cannot be applied. The Di-8-ANEPPS half under reading (b) can be approximated on the pre-exposure 150 and 230 V/cm sets of the 11 cells of 2025-05-01 (88 sets) with two assumptions the criterion does not make: a pixel size of 0.267 um (the iXon Ultra 897's 16 um pixel over the 60x objective, section 2.3; the files give none) and tau of 200 or 300 ns (the tau-radius fit of reference [20] is not available). The notebook's exploratory section gives a through-origin slope of 6.1 to 6.5% dF per 100 mV with a background subtracted and 2.6 to 2.7% without, against 9.1 +- 0.91%, with correlation 0.62 to 0.70 against 0.78. This decides no outcome.

outcomes.statement: FluoVolt measurements became non-linear already at +-200 mV, while Di-8-ANEPPS stayed essentially linear from -500 to +500 mV, so FluoVolt's early departure reflects the limit of the dye's range and not electroporation.
outcomes.quote: The actual measurements with FluoVolt gradually became non-linear already at ±200 mV, while those for Di-8-ANEPPS stayed essentially linear throughout the tested range from −500 to +500 mV.
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig3-dye-slopes, blocked; also needs FluoVolt data.

outcomes.statement: FluoVolt-measured and calculated IMP matched only at 43 and 150 V/cm; with stronger PEFs pole dF reached at most 71 +- 10% (cathodic) and -83.5 +- 5% (anodic), about +260 and -330 mV, and the cathodic value fell from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45 to 50% at 1000 to 1400 V/cm.
outcomes.quote: However, this assumption held only for the applied fields of 43 and 150 V/cm, where measured and calculated IMP matched. With stronger PEFs, maximum ΔF reached 71 ± 10% and −83.5 ± 5% at the cathodic and anodic poles, respectively. ... Notably, polarization at the cathodic pole decreased from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45–50% at 1000–1400 V/cm
outcomes.notes: Needs FluoVolt recordings; every file in the dandiset is Di-8-ANEPPS (its description says so).

outcomes.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS, measured IMP fell below the calculated value when the field reached 570 V/cm, together with the maximum dF of 57 +- 14% at the cathodic pole and -55 +- 4% at the anodic pole, a polarization of over 600 mV, twice that measured with FluoVolt.
outcomes.quote: The measured IMP decreased below the calculated value when the electric field reached 570 V/cm, concurrently with reaching the maximum ΔF of 57 ± 14% at the cathodic pole and − 55 ± 4% at the anodic pole. These values corresponded to membrane polarization by over 600 mV
outcomes.notes: Needs the Di-8-ANEPPS 1 us escalation from 43 to 1400 V/cm (the Fig. 4B group, n = 5); the dandiset holds 1 us recordings only at 150, 230 and 1000 V/cm, in the alternating protocol of Fig. 2C, and the paper's data availability statement says data are available on request.

outcomes.statement: Averaging dF over the first 10 of the 60 PEFs, cathodic pole polarization reached 66 +- 15% (710 +- 200 mV), above the 600 mV maximum averaged over 60 PEFs.
outcomes.quote: Polarization measured this way reached 66 ± 15% (710 ± 200 mV) at the cathodic pole, suggesting that the 600-mV maximum, averaged from 60 PEFs, was not the dye limit but the actual IMP
outcomes.notes: Needs the Di-8-ANEPPS 1 us escalation from 43 to 1400 V/cm (the Fig. 4B group, n = 5); the dandiset holds 1 us recordings only at 150, 230 and 1000 V/cm, in the alternating protocol of Fig. 2C, and the paper's data availability statement says data are available on request.

outcomes.statement: Above 780 V/cm the IMP reached at the poles decreased progressively with field strength, more at the cathodic pole; at 1400 V/cm charging was no longer detectable at the cathodic pole and dropped to about 30% dF (about -330 mV) at the anodic pole.
outcomes.quote: As the electric field increased further, the IMP reached at the poles progressively decreased, and the reduction was more pronounced at the cathodic pole. ... At 1400 V/cm, charging was no longer detectable at the cathodic pole (i.e., the membrane became fully permeable) and dropped to ~30% ΔF (~ −330 mV) at the anodic pole.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Di-8-ANEPPS 1 us escalation from 43 to 1400 V/cm (the Fig. 4B group, n = 5); the dandiset holds 1 us recordings only at 150, 230 and 1000 V/cm, in the alternating protocol of Fig. 2C, and the paper's data availability statement says data are available on request.

outcomes.statement: Membrane regions nearer the equator appeared unaffected and followed the cosine dependence predicted by the Schwan equation up to 1000 V/cm, even when the poles were electroporated.
outcomes.quote: Membrane areas closer to the equator (at polar angles closer to 0◦and 270◦) appeared relatively unaffected and followed the cosine dependence predicted by Schwan formula up to 1000 V/cm (Fig. 4C).
outcomes.notes: Needs the Di-8-ANEPPS 1 us escalation from 43 to 1400 V/cm (the Fig. 4B group, n = 5); the dandiset holds 1 us recordings only at 150, 230 and 1000 V/cm, in the alternating protocol of Fig. 2C, and the paper's data availability statement says data are available on request.

outcomes.statement: 1 mM Gd3+ extended membrane charging at the anodic pole down to -864 +- 44 mV, against -542 +- 57 mV in parallel controls (p < 0.001).
outcomes.quote: Indeed, we found that 1 mM Gd3+ extended the range of membrane charging at the anodic pole down to −864 ± 44 mV (p < 0.001 compared to −542 ± 57 mV in parallel control experiments, Fig. 5A).

statistics.test: t-test (2-tailed t-test in the Fig. 5A legend; Student's t-test in Methods 2.5)
statistics.n: 7 cells with Gd3+ and 5 control cells

outcomes.notes: Needs the Gd3+ (n = 7) and parallel control (n = 5) experiments of Fig. 5A, not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: With Gd3+, measured IMP stayed nearly identical to IMPC down to -780 mV, showing that the Di-8-ANEPPS response stayed linear and its calibration valid at high IMPs.
outcomes.quote: Furthermore, measured IMP remained nearly identical to the theoretical IMPC down to −780 mV, indicating that the dye response remained linear and its calibration was valid even at high IMPs.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Gd3+ (n = 7) and parallel control (n = 5) experiments of Fig. 5A, not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: At the cathodic pole, polarization with Gd3+ reached 647 +- 44 mV, not significantly higher than in controls, but Gd3+ prevented the progressive decline of IMP as field strength increased.
outcomes.quote: At the cathodic pole, polarization in the presence of Gd3+ reached 647 ± 44 mV, a value not significantly higher than that in the control group without Gd3+. However, Gd3+ prevented the progressive decline in IMP as the electric field was increased.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Gd3+ (n = 7) and parallel control (n = 5) experiments of Fig. 5A, not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Differences between Gd3+ and control data are significant at p < 0.05 or better for the datapoints below -700 mV and above 1200 mV.
outcomes.quote: Differences between Gd3+ and control group data are significant at p < 0.05 or better (2-tailed t-test) for datapoints below −700 mV and above 1200 mV.

statistics.n: 7 cells with Gd3+ and 5 control cells

outcomes.notes: Needs the Gd3+ (n = 7) and parallel control (n = 5) experiments of Fig. 5A, not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation-induced effective membrane conductivity 2 to 3 fold.
outcomes.quote: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation- induced effective conductivity 2–3-fold.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Gd3+ (n = 7) and parallel control (n = 5) experiments of Fig. 5A, not in the dandiset. Its dependency fig5b-eq2-sensitivity was tested.

outcomes.statement: A single 1 us pulse at 0 to 1200 V/cm produced a clear Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/cm, with the signal elevated through the 5 min observation; the small increase after 780 V/cm was at the detection limit and not significant.
outcomes.quote: Exposure to a single 1-μs pulse at escalating field strengths, from 0 to 1200 V/cm established a clear peak of Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/ cm, and Ca2+ signal remained elevated through the 5-min observation period (Fig. 6A). A subtle ΔF increase after exposure at 780 V/cm was at the detection limit and not statistically significant.
outcomes.notes: Needs Fluo-4 calcium imaging, not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: With trains of 60 1 us pulses at 6 Hz (224 cells, each tested once), a strong Ca2+ response occurred in 28% of cells at 780 V/cm and nearly all cells at higher fields; at 650 V/cm only 2 cells (5.9%) responded strongly, but the mean signal at the end of recording was significantly above zero (p < 0.001, one-sample t-test) and marginally higher than at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05, single-tailed t-test).
outcomes.quote: A strong Ca2+ response was recorded in 28% of cells exposed at 780 V/cm and in nearly all cells at higher intensities (Fig. 6B). At 650 V/cm, only 2 cells (5.9%) showed a strong response, but the mean Ca2+ signal by the end of recording was significantly different from zero (p < 0.001, one sample t-test) and marginally higher than after exposure at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05, single-tailed t-test).
outcomes.notes: Needs Fluo-4 calcium imaging (224 cells), not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Polarization by a 150 V/cm test pulse 5 us after a conditioning pulse still followed a cosine after conditioning PEFs up to 1000 V/cm, while 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning PEFs markedly hindered charging at the cell poles.
outcomes.quote: Polarization still followed a cosine function after conditioning PEFs of up to 1000 V/cm. However, 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning PEFs markedly hindered charging by the test pulse at cell poles, indicating a persistent membrane permeabilization.
outcomes.notes: Needs the two-pulse (conditioning and 150 V/cm test pulse) experiments of Fig. 7A, not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: During the conditioning pulse, pole polarization normalized to 150 V/cm fell 1.5 times below linear scaling at 560 V/cm, 2-fold at 760 V/cm and further for stronger PEFs (p < 0.01 for all points at 560 V/cm and above, one-sample t-test).
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.7, paragraph 5; Figure 7B, top panel
outcomes.quote: Actual measurements fell 1.5 times below this line for 560 V/cm PEFs, 2- fold for 760 V/cm PEFs, and diverged further for more intense PEFs (p < 0.01 for all datapoints ≥560 V/cm, one sample t-test).
outcomes.notes: Needs the Di-8-ANEPPS 1 us escalation from 43 to 1400 V/cm (the Fig. 4B group, n = 5); the dandiset holds 1 us recordings only at 150, 230 and 1000 V/cm, in the alternating protocol of Fig. 2C, and the paper's data availability statement says data are available on request. Section 3.7 says the top panel of Fig. 7B uses the Fig. 4B data.

outcomes.statement: Polarization by the test pulse 6 us after the conditioning pulse did not differ from control up to 760 V/cm conditioning, was about 80% of control after 1000 V/cm (not significant), and was reduced to about 70% and 50% after 1200 and 1400 V/cm (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01).
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.7, paragraph 5; Figure 7B, bottom panel
outcomes.quote: In contrast, measurements 6 μs later (test pulse) did not differ from the control up to 760 V/cm strength of the conditioning PEF; they were at ~80% of the control reading after 1000 V/cm conditioning PEF but the difference was not statistically significant. Still more intense PEFs of 1200 and 1400 V/cm reduced charging by the test pulse to ~70% and ~ 50%, respectively (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, two-sided t-test).
outcomes.notes: Needs the two-pulse (conditioning and 150 V/cm test pulse) experiments of Fig. 7A, not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Effective membrane conductivity at the poles dropped about 10-fold (range 7 to 20) within 6 us after the electroporating pulse; the cathodic pole was more conductive during the pulse but no pole difference was seen by the test pulse; after 570 and 760 V/cm the membrane resealed fully within 6 us, while stronger PEFs left residual conductivity.
outcomes.quote: Fig. 7C shows a profound reduction in the λm,eff within just 6 μs after the electroporating pulse. For most datapoints, it dropped by a factor of 10 ... 7–20). While the cathodic pole became more conductive than the anodic pole during the electroporating pulse ... no difference between the poles was detected by the test pulse. For mildly electroporating PEFs of 570 and 760 V/cm, membrane resealed fully (within the accuracy of measurements) within just 6 μs.
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig7b-conditioning-sublinear and fig7b-test-pulse-recovery, both blocked for missing data.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the Di-8-ANEPPS experiments of Fig. 2C and D (11 cells) and Fig. 4D (8 cells). The FluoVolt experiments (Fig. 2A, 3, 4A), the Di-8-ANEPPS 1 us escalation (Fig. 1, 2B, 3, 4B, 4C, 7B top), the Gd3+ experiments (Fig. 5), the Fluo-4 calcium imaging (Fig. 6) and the two-pulse experiments (Fig. 7) are not in it; 25 of 30 claims cannot be tested.

The files give pulse amplitudes in volts and no field strengths, while the paper reports every result in V/cm from a Sim4Life model; the mapping (50, 70 and 250 V to 150, 230 and 1000 V/cm; 100 to 800 V to 357 to 3320 V/cm) had to be inferred by order from the paper's figure labels, and the labels are not proportional to the volts (3.0, 3.3 and 4.0 V/cm per volt for 1 us, 3.57 to 4.15 for 0.3 us). A 450 V set (2025-05-06 c1) has no counterpart in Fig. 4D.
The files state an electrode distance of 1.00 mm; the paper (section 2.2) states a 1.6 mm spacing.

Every file carries the same general description, of the 2025-05-01 protocol (50, 70 or 250 V, 13 recordings), including the 2025-05-06 files that hold 0.3 us pulses of 100 to 800 V. The description also calls each recording a single pulse, while each set holds 60 pulsed images, and the dandiset's title and description mention only the post-electroporation experiment.
StrobeImaging starting_time holds Unix times (1746136603 to 1746572254 s), not seconds from session_start_time.
No pixel size is given, so cell radii (needed for IMPC in Eq. 1) are known only in pixels.

Most fields of view hold several cells (one to eight are found), and the files do not say which cell was analysed. The dataset holds 11 cells for the Fig. 2C and D protocol where the paper reports n = 8, and 8 cells for Fig. 4D where it reports n = 10, without saying which cells form the paper's groups. Four of the 11 (2025-05-01 c1, c3, c4 and c11) depart from the order of sets the files' description gives.
In 174 of 232 cell recordings the first image is about 22% darker over the whole frame than the next 39 (median ratio 0.782), which biases F0, defined as the mean of the first 40 images.

Question for the paper's authors. Was a background subtracted from the potentiometric images before computing dF, and if so which: the cell-free background recording made with each 2025-05-01 cell, a cell-free region of the same image, or the camera offset? Section 2.3 describes none; section 2.4 subtracts a cell-free region for Fluo-4. Cell-free background is 52 to 54% of the membrane intensity in these files, so dF without subtraction is about 40% of dF with it. This attempt assumed subtraction of the background recording (and of a cell-free annulus for 2025-05-06). The outcomes of fig2cd-nonelectroporating-stable (not reproduced with subtraction, reproduced without) and fig2c-1000-within-set (reproduced with the background recording only) depend on the answer.

Question for the paper's authors. Which cell in each field of view, and which 8 of the 11 cells of the 2025-05-01 session, form Fig. 2C and D, and are 10 cells of Fig. 4D in the dandiset (it holds 8)? This attempt used the cell nearest the image centre and every cell in the dandiset. Without c3 and c4, the two cells whose pre-exposure sets depart from the described order, all three Fig. 2C and D claims are met; among the 165 choices of 8 cells they are met together in 1 (background recording reading).

Eq. (2) as printed, with the parameters of section 2.3, gives a 1.3% IMP reduction for a 10-fold increase of membrane conductivity, where section 3.5 states ~2% (the 100-fold value, 11.9%, matches the stated 12%).

No dark frame or camera offset is given. The darkest 0.1% of pixels are at about 202 to 208 counts and cell-free regions 65 to 66 counts above them, so how much of the cell-free level is offset and how much stray fluorescence cannot be told from the files. If the darkest pixels are the offset, fig2c-1000-within-set is not met (start 24.0%) and fig2cd-nonelectroporating-stable is not reproduced (p = 0.038).

entries.name: semenov-2026-001526
entries.title: Membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields in CHO cells (Semenov et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Silkuniene, Silkunas, Pakhomova, Bixler, Ibey, Kochunov and Pakhomov (2026) on dandiset 001526, which holds Di-8-ANEPPS strobe images of 19 CHO cells, the alternating 150 and 230 V/cm protocol around a 1000 V/cm exposure (Fig. 2C and D) and the 0.3 us escalation (Fig. 4D). It traces each cell's membrane, measures pole dF per image and per set, and evaluates Eq. (2). The FluoVolt, 1 us escalation, Gd3+, Ca2+ and two-pulse experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Semenov et al. (2026) from dandiset 001526
